name: evidence-artifact-store-atomic-writes
title: Evidence artifact store: non-atomic immutable-object write plus exists-then-read dedupe can permanently poison a digest (F-012 TOCTOU-class audit follow-up)
description: B-70e9's F-012 fixed a read-last-hash-then-append race in the usage ledger with an mkdir lock. A repo-wide follow-up audit of every appendFileSync / last-line-dependent JSONL writer under packages/main/src found no second hash-chained tail-dependent appender, but found one same-family integrity defect: packages/main/src/core/evidence/artifact-store.ts writeArtifact() writes the 'immutable' content-addressed object objects/sha256/<digest>.json with a plain non-atomic writeFileSync, and its dedupe path is existsSync -> readFileSync -> JSON.parse -> return. A crash or kill mid-write leaves a truncated object file, after which every writeArtifact call for the same content takes the exists branch and throws on JSON.parse forever: the write branch is skipped because the file exists, so the store never self-heals. Concurrent same-digest writers (repro-intake CLI commands invoked by the main agent and subagents run outside the validate execution lock) can hit the same window transiently. Repro-intake artifacts feed the repro-evidence-binding DEV gate, so a poisoned digest blocks a story until someone hand-deletes files under .lattice/evidence/objects/.

riskSignalsDismissed.reason: False positive: the word truncate appears only in a regression-test description (simulate a crash-truncated JSON object file under .lattice/evidence/objects/ to verify self-healing). The story modifies no schema, no migration, and deletes no user data; it makes evidence-store writes atomic (tmp+renameSync) in packages/main/src/core/evidence/artifact-store.ts.
